title: Do not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk
original_audience: Israelites preparing a lamb or young animal in the setting of the covenant ordinances

original_audience: Israel settling the land, regarding the specified inhabitants and their worship

verse_text: [23:33] neither shall they dwell in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me; for if you serve their gods, these shall be a stumbling block to you.”
maimonides: N51: Do not let idolaters dwell in the land

original_audience: The Israelites supplying the oil under Moses' formal charge
verse_text: [27:20] You shall command the sons of Israel to bring you pure beaten olive oil, free of sediment, for the light, so that a lamp may burn continually

title: Priests: maintain the sanctuary lamps from evening to morning
original_audience: Aaron and his sons attending the sanctuary lamps for Israel
verse_text: [27:21] in the Tent of Testimony, outside the veil over the covenant. Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening to morning before the Lord, a perpetual statute throughout your generations on behalf of the sons of Israel.”
maimonides: P25: Kindle the sanctuary lamps daily

title: High priest: wear the sounding robe when ministering in the sanctuary
original_audience: Aaron as high priest entering and leaving the sanctuary during ministry

title: Priests: wear the covering undergarments when entering or ministering
original_audience: Aaron, his sons, and their priestly descendants entering the tent or approaching the altar

maimonides: P33: Priests wear the priestly garments during their service

title: Give the appointed sacrificial portions to the priests
original_audience: Israelites contributing the designated portions to Aaron and his sons
verse_text: [29:27] Consecrate the breast set apart and the foreleg of the contribution, which were set apart and taken from the ram of consecration for Aaron and his sons. [29:28] And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons by an everlasting statute from the sons of Israel; for it is a contribution, and shall be a contribution from the sons of Israel, from their sacrifices of deliverance, a contribution to the Lord.

title: Transfer the high priest's holy garments to his successor
original_audience: The priests of Aaron's line inheriting the sacred vestments
verse_text: [29:29] Aaron’s holy robe shall belong to his sons after him, to be anointed in the garments and have their hands consecrated. [29:30] The priest who succeeds him from among his sons shall wear them for seven days; he shall enter the Tent of Testimony to minister in the holy places.

title: Do not allow outsiders to eat the consecration meal
original_audience: Outsiders barred from the consecration meal, with those serving the meal responsible for the boundary
verse_text: [29:33] They shall eat the things by which they were sanctified, to consecrate their hands and sanctify them. An outsider shall not eat them, because they are holy.
maimonides: N149: A non-priest must not eat the most holy offerings

title: Do not eat the consecration leftovers after the appointed time
original_audience: Those who would eat consecration food remaining until morning
verse_text: [29:34] And if any of the flesh of the consecration sacrifice, or of the bread, remains until morning, you shall burn the remainder with fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is a holy thing.

title: Offer the daily morning and evening lambs with the prescribed grain, oil and wine
original_audience: Moses as the formal addressee and the appointed sanctuary priests for the continuing daily offering
verse_text: [29:38] This is what you shall offer on the altar: two year-old lambs without blemish each day continually, a continual offering. [29:39] Offer one lamb in the morning and the second in the evening. [29:40] With one lamb offer a tenth measure of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of beaten oil, and a quarter hin of wine as a libation. [29:41] Offer the second lamb in the evening, with the same sacrifice and libation as in the morning, as a fragrant aroma, an offering to the Lord, [29:42] as a continual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony before the Lord, where I will be made known to you, to speak to you.
maimonides: P39: Offer the two daily (tamid) lambs

maimonides: P28: Burn incense on the golden altar every morning and evening

title: Do not offer unauthorized incense on the incense altar

original_audience: Aaron as high priest, and the priestly office continuing the annual purification
verse_text: [30:10] Once a year Aaron shall make expiation for it on its horns. With the blood of purification for sins, for expiation, once a year he shall purify it throughout their generations. It is most holy to the Lord.

title: Give the equal prescribed census ransom for each counted adult male
original_audience: Each Israelite counted from age twenty upward, whether rich or poor
verse_text: [30:12] “When you number the sons of Israel in their visitation, each shall give the Lord a ransom for his soul, and no downfall shall come among them in their visitation. [30:13] This is what all who pass into the numbering shall give: half a didrachma, according to the holy didrachma. Twenty obols make the didrachma, and half a didrachma shall be the contribution to the Lord. [30:14] Everyone counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the contribution to the Lord. [30:15] The rich shall give no more and the poor no less than half a didrachma when giving the contribution to the Lord to make propitiation for your lives.
maimonides: P171: Give the half-shekel to the sanctuary each year

title: Priests: wash hands and feet before sanctuary entry or altar ministry

verse_text: [30:19] Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and feet with water from it. [30:20] When they enter the Tent of Testimony, they shall wash with water so that they do not die. When they approach the altar to minister and offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord, [30:21] they shall wash their hands and feet with water. When they enter the Tent of Testimony, they shall wash with water so that they do not die. This shall be a perpetual statute for him and his generations after him.”
maimonides: P24: Priests wash hands and feet before sanctuary service

[31:16] The sons of Israel shall keep the Sabbaths, observing them throughout their generations: an everlasting covenant. [31:17] It is an everlasting sign between Me and the sons of Israel, for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and rested.’”
maimonides: P154: Rest on the Sabbath

Whoever does work on it, that soul shall be destroyed from among his people. [31:15] For six days you shall do your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord. Whoever does work on the seventh day shall surely be put to death.

It is a sacrifice. [2:16] And the priest shall offer up its memorial portion, some of the groats with the oil and all its frankincense. It is an offering unto the Lord.

title: Present an unblemished animal of the prescribed kinds for a peace or deliverance offering

P69: An individual brings a sin offering for an inadvertent transgression

title: Disclose relevant testimony when solemnly called as a witness
original_audience: Israelite witness under solemn adjuration
verse_text: [5:1] And if a soul sins, and hears the voice of a solemn adjuration, and he is a witness, whether he has seen or has knowledge of the matter, if he does not declare it, he shall bear the sin.
maimonides: P178: Testify in court when one has relevant knowledge

title: Confess the offense in the stated witness, impurity, or oath cases
original_audience: Israelite who incurs the stated guilt
context_note: Verse 5 requires confession of the fault in the cases laid out in verses 1–4. The specified remedies follow in verses 6–13.
verse_text: [5:1] And if a soul sins, and hears the voice of a solemn adjuration, and he is a witness, whether he has seen or has knowledge of the matter, if he does not declare it, he shall bear the sin. [5:2] Or if a soul touches any unclean thing, whether a dead thing, or an unclean thing torn by wild beasts, or one of the dead things, or one of the unclean abominations, or a carcass of unclean livestock, [5:3] or touches human uncleanness, any uncleanness of a man by touching which he is defiled, and it escapes his notice, but afterward he knows it and incurs guilt; [5:4] or if a soul swears, declaring with his lips to do evil or to do good, whatsoever a man declares with an oath, and it escapes his notice, and he knows it and sins in any one of these matters, [5:5] he shall confess the sin concerning that wherein he has sinned.
maimonides: P73: Confess one's sin before God

title: Bring the prescribed offering for the stated witness, impurity and oath offences, with poverty substitutions
original_audience: Israelite liable for one of the listed offences
verse_text: [5:6] And he shall bring unto the Lord, for the offence and the sin which he has committed, a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a female young goat from the goats, for sin. And the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin which he has committed, and his sin shall be forgiven him. [5:7] And if his hand cannot provide enough for a sheep, he shall bring unto the Lord for the sin which he has committed two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering.

maimonides: N102: Do not put oil on the sinner's meal offering
N103: Do not put frankincense on the sinner's meal offering

original_audience: Officiating Aaronic priest

maimonides: P118: Repay misused sacred property plus a fifth

original_audience: Aaron and his sons
context_note: The remainder is allotted to Aaron and his sons, who eat it unleavened in the designated holy place. Verse 10 expressly forbids baking that portion with leaven.
verse_text: [6:9] But Aaron and his sons shall eat what remains of it. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they shall eat it in the court of the Tent of Testimony. [6:10] It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it unto them as a portion from the offerings of the Lord; it is most holy, as the offering for sin and the guilt offering.
maimonides: N124: Do not bake the meal-offering remainder with leaven

title: Burn a priest’s grain offering entirely and do not eat it
original_audience: Aaron and his sons as priests
context_note: Leviticus 6:16 requires a priest’s grain offering to be burned completely and expressly forbids eating it. Other grain offerings have separately assigned priestly portions.
verse_text: [6:16] And every sacrifice of a priest shall be wholly burned, and shall not be eaten.
maimonides: N138: Do not eat a priest's meal offering

title: Eligible priests: eat the designated sin offering in the holy court
original_audience: Officiating priest and eligible male Aaronic priests
verse_text: [6:19] The priest who offers it up shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Testimony.
maimonides: P89: Priests eat the meat of the sin and guilt offerings
N145: Priests must not eat sin or guilt offerings outside the court

title: Do not eat the sin offering whose blood was brought inside the sanctuary
original_audience: Aaron and his sons as priests
verse_text: [6:23] And none of the offerings for sin whose blood is brought into the Tent of Testimony to make atonement in the holy place shall be eaten; they shall be burned with fire.
maimonides: N139: Do not eat sin offerings whose blood enters the Sanctuary

title: Eligible priests: eat the guilt offering in a holy place
original_audience: Eligible male Aaronic priests
verse_text: [7:6] Every male among the priests shall eat them; they shall eat them in a holy place. They are most holy. [7:7] As the offering for sin, so also the guilt offering: one law is theirs. It shall belong unto the priest who makes atonement with it.
maimonides: P89: Priests eat the meat of the sin and guilt offerings
N145: Priests must not eat sin or guilt offerings outside the court

title: Give the burnt offering hide to the officiating priest
original_audience: Officiating priest who brings the burnt offering
verse_text: [7:8] And the priest who brings a man’s whole burnt offering shall have the hide of the whole burnt offering which he brings.

title: Give oven- and pan-cooked grain offerings to the officiating priest
original_audience: Aaron and his sons
context_note: the Lord through Moses addresses Aaron and his sons in this passage.
verse_text: [7:9] And every sacrifice made in an oven, and every sacrifice made upon a hearth or upon a griddle, shall belong unto the priest who brings it.

title: Share grain offerings prepared with or without oil equally among Aaron's sons
original_audience: Aaron and his sons
context_note: The text explicitly mentions grain offerings prepared with or without oil and an equal share for each of Aaron's sons.
verse_text: [7:10] And every sacrifice prepared with oil, or not so prepared, shall belong unto all the sons of Aaron, unto each an equal share.

title: Bring the prescribed breads with the thanksgiving peace offering
original_audience: Israelite bringing a thanksgiving peace offering
verse_text: [7:12] If he brings it for praise, he shall bring with the sacrifice of praise loaves of fine flour prepared with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour mixed with oil. [7:13] He shall bring his gifts with leavened loaves, with a sacrifice of praise and deliverance.

title: Eat the thanksgiving peace offering that day and leave none until morning
original_audience: Offerer and other eligible participants
context_note: Leviticus 7:15 states one consumption deadline in positive and negative terms. Leviticus 22:30 repeats the same-day rule.
verse_text: [7:15] And the flesh of the sacrifice of praise and deliverance shall be his, and shall be eaten on the day when it is given; they shall leave none of it until morning.
maimonides: N120: Do not leave thanksgiving-offering meat until morning

title: Eat vow or freewill peace-offering meat within two days
original_audience: Offerer and other eligible participants
context_note: Leviticus 7:16 permits eating on the offering day and the next day. Verse 18 excludes eating on the third day and gives the stated consequence. The separate instruction to burn leftovers remains in C0452.
verse_text: [7:16] And if he sacrifices his gift as a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day when he brings his sacrifice, and on the morrow. [7:17] And what remains of the flesh of the sacrifice until the third day shall be burned with fire. [7:18] But if he eats any of the flesh on the third day, it shall not be accepted for him who brings it, neither shall it be reckoned unto him; it is a defilement. And the soul that eats of it shall bear the sin.
maimonides: N131: Do not eat sacrificial meat left beyond its time (notar)
N132: Do not eat piggul, an offering invalidated by improper intent

title: Do not eat sacrificial flesh that has touched uncleanness
original_audience: Potential eaters of sacrificial flesh
verse_text: [7:19] And flesh which touches any unclean thing shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. Whosoever is clean shall eat flesh.
maimonides: N130: Do not eat sacrificial meat that has become unclean

title: Do not eat the holy peace offering while unclean
original_audience: Israelites in ritual uncleanness
verse_text: [7:20] But the soul that eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of deliverance which is the Lord’s, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall perish from among his people. [7:21] And if a soul touches any unclean thing, human uncleanness, or unclean four-footed beasts, or any unclean abomination, and eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of deliverance which is the Lord’s, that soul shall perish from among his people.
maimonides: N129: An unclean person must not eat sacrificial food

title: Do not eat the fat of animals found dead or torn
original_audience: the sons of Israel
context_note: Using this fat for work is permitted. Eating it is prohibited.
verse_text: [7:24] And fat from animals that have died, or from those torn by wild beasts, may be used for any work; but it shall in no wise be eaten as food.

title: Allot the right foreleg to the priest who presents the blood and fat
original_audience: the sons of Israel
context_note: Verse 33 identifies the particular priest entitled to the right foreleg. The surrounding verses describe the general priestly portions.
verse_text: [7:33] He among the sons of Aaron who brings the blood of the offering of deliverance and the fat shall have the right foreleg as his portion.

title: Priests: drink no wine or strong drink when entering the tent or approaching the altar
original_audience: Aaron and his sons as priests
verse_text: [10:9] You shall drink no wine or strong drink, you and your sons with you, when you enter the Tent of Testimony, or when you approach the altar, so that you do not die: an everlasting statute throughout your generations,
maimonides: N73: A priest must not enter the Sanctuary or serve intoxicated

title: Priests: distinguish holy from profane and clean from unclean
original_audience: Aaron and his sons as priests
verse_text: [10:10] to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.

title: Priests: teach Israel God's statutes
original_audience: Aaron and his sons as priests
verse_text: [10:11] And you shall instruct the sons of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord spoke unto them by the hand of Moses.

title: Eat the breast and foreleg in a holy place with your household
original_audience: Aaron, Eleazar and Ithamar
context_note: Moses relays the Lord's direction to Aaron and his remaining sons. The Saints Translation says holy place, and verse 15 includes sons and daughters.
verse_text: [10:14] And you shall eat the breast of the separated portion and the foreleg of the portion set apart in a holy place, you and your sons and your house with you; for it was given as your prescribed portion and the prescribed portion of your sons from the sacrifices of deliverance of the sons of Israel. [10:15] They shall bring the foreleg of the portion set apart and the breast of the separated portion with the offerings of fat, to set apart a separated portion before the Lord; and it shall be an everlasting prescribed portion for you, and for your sons and your daughters with you, as the Lord directed Moses.

title: Do not eat land animals excluded by the prescribed hoof and cud criteria
original_audience: Israel
context_note: Christians differ about the reach of these passages. Acts 15:19–29 must also be read; the instruction concerning blood is treated separately.
verse_text: [11:2] Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: These are the animals you may eat among all the animals on the earth. [11:3] Every animal among the livestock that divides the hoof, and cleaves its claws into two hoofs, and brings up the cud: these you may eat. [11:4] Nevertheless, of these you shall not eat: among those that bring up the cud and those that divide the hoof and cleave the claws, the camel, because it brings up the cud, but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean unto you; [11:5] and the hare, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you; [11:6] and the choirogryllios, because it brings up the cud but does not divide the hoof; it is unclean for you; [11:7] and the pig, because it divides the hoof and has cleft hoof-claws but does not bring up the cud; it is unclean for you. [11:8] You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
maimonides: P149: Examine land animals for the kosher signs: split hoof, cud
N172: Do not eat unclean land animals

title: Do not touch the prohibited animal carcasses
original_audience: Israel
verse_text: [11:8] You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
maimonides: P96: Observe the impurity laws of animal carcasses (nevelah)

title: Do not eat water creatures lacking fins and scales
original_audience: Israel
context_note: Christians differ about the reach of these passages. Acts 15:19–29 must also be read; the instruction concerning blood is treated separately.
verse_text: [11:9] And these you may eat among all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and streams, you may eat. [11:10] And whatever has neither fins nor scales in the water, in the seas and streams, among all that the waters bring forth and every living creature in the water, is an abomination. [11:11] And they shall be abominations for you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall abhor their carcasses. [11:12] And whatever among the things in the water has no fins and scales is an abomination for you.
maimonides: P152: Examine fish for the kosher signs: fins and scales
N173: Do not eat non-kosher fish

title: Do not eat the prohibited birds listed in the law
original_audience: Israel
context_note: Christians differ about the reach of these passages. Acts 15:19–29 must also be read; the instruction concerning blood is treated separately.
verse_text: [11:13] And these you shall abhor among the birds; they shall not be eaten, for they are an abomination: the eagle, the gryps, and the sea-eagle; [11:14] and the vulture, the kite, and those like it; [11:15] and the raven and those like it; [11:16] and the ostrich, the owl, the gull and those like it, and the hawk and those like it; [11:17] and the night-raven, the diving bird, and the ibis; [11:18] and the purple waterbird, the pelican, and the swan; [11:19] and the owl, the heron, the plover and those like it, the hoopoe, and the bat.
maimonides: N174: Do not eat non-kosher birds

title: Do not eat prohibited winged insects, observing the stated locust exceptions
original_audience: Israel
context_note: Christians differ about the reach of these passages. Acts 15:19–29 must also be read; the instruction concerning blood is treated separately.
verse_text: [11:20] And every winged creeping thing that walks on four is an abomination for you. [11:21] But among the winged creeping things that walk on four, you may eat those that have legs above their feet for leaping on the earth. [11:22] And these among them you may eat: the brouchos and those like it, the attakes and those like it, the locust and those like it, and the snake-fighter and those like it. [11:23] Every winged creeping thing that has four feet is an abomination for you.
maimonides: P151: Examine locusts for the kosher signs
N175: Do not eat unclean flying insects

title: Observe the prescribed uncleanness until evening after carcass contact
original_audience: Israelites who touch or carry the specified carcasses
verse_text: [11:24] And by these you shall become defiled: everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening, [11:25] and whosoever carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. [11:26] Every animal that divides the hoof and has cleft claws but does not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening. [11:27] And among all wild animals that walk on four, whatever walks on its hands shall be unclean for you. Whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening. [11:28] And whosoever carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you. [11:29] And these are unclean for you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the land crocodile; [11:30] the shrew, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole. [11:31] These are unclean for you among all the creeping things on the earth. Whosoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.
maimonides: P96: Observe the impurity laws of animal carcasses (nevelah)
P97: Observe the impurity of the eight creeping creatures

title: Apply the stated carcass-contamination rules to objects, food, water, and seed
original_audience: Israelites handling food, drink, vessels, or seed
verse_text: [11:32] And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall become unclean: any wooden utensil, garment, skin, or sack, any article used for work. It shall be dipped in water and remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean. [11:33] And if one of them falls inside any earthenware vessel, everything in it shall become unclean, and the vessel shall be shattered. [11:34] And any food that may be eaten, on which water comes, shall become unclean, and any drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall become unclean. [11:35] And anything on which any of their carcasses falls shall become unclean. Ovens and pot-stands shall be demolished; these are unclean and shall be unclean for you. [11:36] But springs of water, a cistern, and a gathering of water shall remain clean; whosoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean. [11:37] If any of their carcasses falls on seed intended for sowing, it remains clean. [11:38] But if water is poured on any seed and any of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
maimonides: P98: Food and drink become susceptible to impurity through liquids

title: Do not eat or defile yourselves with the prohibited ground-creeping creatures
original_audience: Israel
context_note: Christians differ about the reach of these passages. Acts 15:19–29 must also be read; the instruction concerning blood is treated separately.
verse_text: [11:41] And every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth shall be an abomination for you; it shall not be eaten. [11:42] And whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on four continually, whatever has many feet among all the creeping things that creep upon the earth, you shall not eat, for it is an abomination for you. [11:43] And you shall in no wise make your souls abominable through any creeping things that creep upon the earth; neither shall you be defiled through them, nor shall you be unclean through them; [11:44] for I am the Lord your God; and you shall be sanctified and you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God. And you shall not defile your souls through any creeping things that move upon the earth;
maimonides: N176: Do not eat swarming creatures of the land
N177: Do not eat creeping things that breed in decaying matter
N178: Do not eat worms found in fruit once they emerge
N179: Do not eat any swarming creature, including small water creatures

title: Observe the prescribed uncleanness and purification periods after childbirth
original_audience: Israelite woman after childbirth
context_note: The chapter gives initial uncleanness and further purification periods for births of sons and daughters. The eighth-day circumcision clause and the sanctuary restrictions have separate scope.
verse_text: [12:2] Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a woman receives seed and bears a male, she shall be unclean seven days; she shall be unclean as in the days of separation for her menstrual discharge. [12:4] And she shall remain thirty-three days in her unclean blood. She shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed. [12:5] But if she bears a female, she shall be unclean twice seven days according to her menstrual discharge; and she shall remain sixty-six days in her unclean blood.
maimonides: P100: Observe the impurity laws of a woman after childbirth

title: Do not touch holy things during postpartum purification
original_audience: Israelite woman undergoing postpartum purification
verse_text: [12:4] And she shall remain thirty-three days in her unclean blood. She shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
maimonides: N129: An unclean person must not eat sacrificial food

title: Do not enter the sanctuary before postpartum purification is completed
original_audience: Israelite woman undergoing postpartum purification
verse_text: [12:4] And she shall remain thirty-three days in her unclean blood. She shall touch nothing holy and shall not enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
maimonides: N77: An impure person must not enter the sanctuary camp

title: Bring the prescribed childbirth purification offerings, including the poverty provision
original_audience: Israelite woman completing postpartum purification
context_note: This clause from Luke independently supports Leviticus 12:6–8.
verse_text: [12:6] And when the days of her purification for a son or daughter are completed, she shall bring unto the priest at the door of the Tent of Testimony an unblemished year-old lamb for a whole burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for sin. [12:7] And the priest shall present it before the Lord, and make atonement for her, and cleanse her from the fountain of her blood. This is the law for her that bears a male or a female. [12:8] If her hand cannot provide enough for a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a whole burnt offering and one for sin. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be cleansed.
maimonides: P76: A woman after childbirth brings her purification offerings

title: Declare skin and scalp lesions clean or unclean by their prescribed criteria
original_audience: Examining Aaronic priest
context_note: Leviticus 13 distinguishes the initial skin lesion from an old lesion, changes in raw flesh, a healed ulcer or burn, scalp or beard lesions, and ordinary white eruptions or baldness. The result depends on the criteria prescribed for each case.
verse_text: [13:3] And the priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair in the lesion has turned white and the lesion appears lower than the skin of his body, it is a lesion of leprosy. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.
maimonides: P101: Observe the laws of skin-disease impurity in a person
